Assurance of Faith
uh-SHOOR-ance of FAITH
noun / doctrine
The believer’s “full assurance of faith” (Heb 10:22), the settled certainty of his interest in Christ by the witness of the Spirit.

Biblical Definition

Assurance of faith is the settled certainty a believer may attain that he is indeed in a state of grace, accepted in Christ, and an heir of eternal life. It is no presumption, but a grace held out in Scripture and to be diligently sought. The Apostle bids us “draw near with a true heart in full assurance of faith” (Heb 10:22), and witnesses that “the Spirit itself beareth witness with our spirit, that we are the children of God” (Rom 8:16). John wrote his Epistle for this very end: “These things have I written unto you that believe on the name of the Son of God; that ye may know that ye have eternal life” (1Jo 5:13). And Peter exhorts, “give diligence to make your calling and election sure” (2Pe 1:10), joining assurance to a holy and fruitful walk. The 1689 Confession teaches that this certain assurance does not so belong to the essence of faith but that a true believer may wait long and conflict with many difficulties before he obtain it; it is founded on the blood and righteousness of Christ, the inward evidence of the graces of the Spirit, and the testimony of the Spirit of adoption. It may be shaken and intermitted by negligence or by falling into sin, yet the believer is never utterly destitute of that seed of God and life of faith by which it may in due time be revived. Assurance, rightly held, fills the heart with peace, love, and holy obedience.

Webster 1828 Definition

The settled certainty a believer may attain of his interest in Christ, founded on Christ’s work, the Spirit’s witness, and the fruit of grace.

ASSURANCE OF FAITH, the believer’s settled certainty of his interest in Christ.

We may draw near in full assurance of faith (Heb 10:22).

The Spirit beareth witness that we are the children of God (Rom 8:16).

John wrote that believers may know they have eternal life (1Jo 5:13).

We are bidden to make our calling and election sure (2Pe 1:10).

Key Scripture

Heb 10:22 — "Let us draw near with a true heart in full assurance of faith, having our hearts sprinkled from an evil conscience, and our bodies washed with pure water."

Rom 8:16 — "The Spirit itself beareth witness with our spirit, that we are the children of God:"

1Jo 5:13 — "These things have I written unto you that believe on the name of the Son of God; that ye may know that ye have eternal life, and that ye may believe on the name of the Son of God."

2Pe 1:10 — "Wherefore the rather, brethren, give diligence to make your calling and election sure: for if ye do these things, ye shall never fall."

Modern Corruption

Assurance is corrupted from two sides: a presumptuous easy-believism that grants false peace without fruit, and a morbid introspection that denies the believer the comfort God holds out.

expand to see more

On one side stands presumptuous easy-believism, which grants a hollow assurance on the strength of a past decision or a bare profession, while the life shows no fruit of repentance or holiness. This is a false peace, a carnal security that flatters the unconverted and forgets that Peter joins assurance to a diligent and fruitful walk: “give diligence to make your calling and election sure” (2Pe 1:10). True assurance is never severed from a holy life; the man who says he knows Christ and keeps not His commandments is a liar, and the false comfort that soothes him to sleep in his sins is among the cruelest of errors.

On the other side stands a morbid introspection, which so turns the eye inward upon the soul’s remaining corruption that it denies the believer the comfort God Himself holds out. Such a soul, ever doubting, ever digging for evidences and finding only sin, robs itself of the peace Christ purchased and dishonours the Spirit who witnesses with our spirit that we are God’s children. The 1689 Confession (ch. 18) answers both errors: assurance does not so belong to the essence of faith but that a true believer may wait long before he obtain it, yet it is a real grace, founded on Christ’s blood, the Spirit’s witness, and the inward graces, to be diligently sought and never presumed nor needlessly despaired of.

Hebrew Roots

From the “full assurance of faith” (Heb 10:22), the believer’s certainty of his interest in Christ.

expand to see more

Assurance of faith — the believer’s certainty of his state in grace.

It is founded on the blood and righteousness of Christ.

It rests on the witness of the Spirit of adoption (Rom 8:16).

It is confirmed by the inward graces and a holy walk (2Pe 1:10).

The 1689 Confession (ch. 18) is the dictionary’s standard.

Usage

"Seek a true assurance founded on Christ, the Spirit’s witness, and the fruit of grace, never on a bare profession."

"Reject the false peace of easy-believism that grants comfort without repentance or holiness."

"Reject the morbid introspection that denies the believer the comfort God holds out in His Word."
